name: Inuit Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Schuit, Joke (2014), 'Signs of the Arctic: Typological aspects of Inuit Sign Language', PhD thesis, Univ. of Amsterdam — the descriptive work on IUR; sign modality, word stress in the spoken sense unlikely

sources.citation: Schuit, Joke M. (2014). Signs of the Arctic: Typological aspects of Inuit Sign Language. PhD thesis, Universiteit van Amsterdam. ix+189 pp. (UvA-DARE, hdl.handle.net/11245/1.404611; chapter-wise PDFs)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Section 2.1 'Phonological aspects' (pp. 26-37) treats only handshape, location/signing space and the non-manual parameter; nothing on stress, prosody, rhythm or accent anywhere in the thesis (all chapter text layers a full-text search for stress/accent). The author states no phonological analysis is attempted (p. 26) and 'No thorough phonological analysis has been undertaken' (p. 29).

sources.citation: Schuit, Joke (2012). Signing in the Arctic: External influences on Inuit Sign Language. In U. Zeshan & C. de Vos (eds), Sign Languages in Village Communities, 181-208. De Gruyter Mouton / Ishara Press.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Largely duplicated by thesis ch. 5 (which is the one chapter NOT served on UvA-DARE); would close the gap on the unread chapter, though a stress statement is very unlikely.

sources.citation: Schuit, Joke, Anne Baker & Roland Pfau (2011). Inuit Sign Language: a contribution to sign language typology. Linguistics in Amsterdam 4(1): 1-31.
sources.note: Verb agreement and classifiers only; no phonology/prosody section, no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Schuit, Joke (2015). Inuit Sign Language. In J. B. Jepsen, G. de Clerck, S. Lutalo-Kiingi & W. B. McGregor (eds), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 431-448. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
